faq.a: No. DishaYaaN is a mentorship and future-readiness platform. Exam preparation is one layer of it; exploration, projects, career discovery and human mentorship sit alongside it.

faq.q: Which classes do you work with?
faq.a: Students from Class 6 to Class 12. Exploration tracks start from Class 6, technology labs from around Class 7–8, and exam pathways from Class 9 upwards.

faq.q: What exactly can my child explore in v1?
faq.a: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Robotics, Drone Technology, Computer Science, Stock Market & Trading, plus Biotechnology, Physics, Engineering, Research and Entrepreneurship exploration tracks.

faq.q: Does the Path Finder predict my future?
faq.a: It does not, and we will never claim that. It is an exploration tool: it shows which areas you may enjoy exploring next and gives a mentor something concrete to talk with you about.

faq.q: How does the AI assistant relate to a real mentor?
faq.a: DishaYaaN AI helps you explore quickly and asks the right context questions. It never replaces a human mentor — every AI conversation ends with an option to talk to a person.

faq.q: What do parents actually get to see?
faq.a: A progress view covering sessions attended, projects in flight, mentor feedback, skills being built and the next recommended step. Parents see the same roadmap the student does.
Plans are billed monthly, with a one-time option for the twelve-week Goal Sprint. You pay online from the Plans page and receive a receipt; nothing is charged without your knowledge.

faq.q: How do bookings and scheduling work?
faq.a: Pick a domain, a format and a slot on the booking page. The request lands with the mentor-matching team, you get a confirmation on WhatsApp, and the session appears in your dashboard with everything the mentor already knows about you.

faq.q: Can students publish their own work?
faq.a: Yes. Every learner can post an update, upload a file or an image, and comment on other students' posts in the community area. Posts are visible to the DishaYaaN community and to mentors.

faq.q: Who can see my work and my conversations?
faq.a: Your posts are visible to the community and to mentors. Your private sessions, bookings and payment records are visible only to you, your mentor and the DishaYaaN team.

faq.q: We are a school or coaching centre. Can we partner?
faq.a: Yes. DishaYaaN runs alongside institutions as an add-on lab, a mentor pool or a future-readiness programme. Send a requirement through the partnership form and we will scope it with you.

faq.q: What if the plan is not right for us?
faq.a: Tell us inside the first seven days and we will refund the current period. We would rather fix the mismatch than keep a fee that is not earning its place.

project_examples.title: Sign-language letter recogniser
project_examples.problem: A student wanted a way for their younger sibling to practise sign-language letters without a teacher present.
project_examples.solution: A camera-based classifier that recognises hand shapes and shows the letter with a confidence score.
project_examples.learned: Data quality matters more than model choice — the first dataset was unusable.

project_examples.title: Line-following rover with sensor fusion
project_examples.problem: A rover kept losing the track on curves because a single sensor was not enough.
project_examples.solution: Three sensors combined with a weighted control rule, tuned with a mentor over four sessions.
project_examples.learned: Debugging is a method, not luck. The build log showed exactly where it drifted.

project_examples.title: Village mapping flight plan
project_examples.problem: A student wanted to understand how aerial surveys are actually planned for real terrain.
project_examples.solution: A simulated mapping mission with waypoints, altitude bands, overlap percentage and a safety checklist.
project_examples.learned: Regulation and safety come before flying — and they are part of the engineering.

project_examples.title: A paper-trading portfolio with a written thesis
project_examples.problem: A student was interested in markets but had no process beyond looking at price movement.
project_examples.solution: A five-stock paper portfolio with research notes, position sizing rules and a weekly review sheet.
project_examples.learned: Writing down why you bought something is the whole discipline.

hero.title: Why DishaYaaN exists.
hero.lead: Traditional academics matter — and they are not enough on their own. A student can score well and still have no idea what they enjoy, what they are good at, or what the world they are stepping into actually looks like.
gap_list: A human who has done the work

hero.gap_closing: DishaYaaN exists to close that gap without pretending school does not matter.

vision.label: Our vision
vision.title: Every student should be able to name three futures they would genuinely want — before they are asked to choose one.
vision.body: Not by predicting anything, and not by selling reassurance. By giving students real exposure, real mentors and real projects, then helping them build a plan they can defend.

problem.label: The problem
paragraphs: Most students in Class 6–12 receive two inputs: a syllabus and exam pressure. Exposure to technology, careers and research usually arrives either too late or only for students with well-connected families.
Meanwhile the fields that will shape their twenties — AI, machine learning, robotics, drones, biotech, financial markets — are either invisible in school or reduced to a single computer period.
problem.emphasis: The result is bright students choosing a path by elimination rather than by desire.

approach.title: Discover. Learn. Build. Achieve.
approach.lead: Four verbs, in that order. Discovery before curriculum, projects before certificates, and a plan before any payment.

steps.body: Interests, subjects and what you actually enjoy doing after school hours.

Something real in every track: a robot, a model, a drone mission, a research note, a portfolio.
Progress reviewed against your goal charter, with the roadmap updated as you grow.

philosophy.title: How we operate, stated plainly.
philosophy.lead: These are commitments, not slogans. They are the reason some sections of this site currently look empty — the real ones come later.

items.title: We do not invent proof
items.body: No fake testimonials, no borrowed logos, no rank claims. Anything on this site is either true today or explicitly marked as a placeholder.

items.title: Mentors are people, not content
items.body: A mentor's job is to look at your specific situation and tell you the truth, including when your current plan is wrong.

items.title: AI assists; humans decide
items.body: DishaYaaN AI narrows the field quickly. A person then helps you choose a direction and stay with it.

items.title: Parents are partners
items.body: A parent who can see the plan can support it. Visibility is a feature, not a privilege.

audiences.title: Students, parents and mentors are treated as three different products.

items.title: How we think about students
items.body: You are not a syllabus to be covered. You are someone with curiosity, limited time and real pressure from school. DishaYaaN tries to make exploration cheap — one hour a week that widens what you think is possible for yourself.

items.title: How we think about parents
items.body: You deserve to know what happens after school hours without interrogating your child. You get the same roadmap, attendance and mentor notes they do, in plain language.

items.title: How we think about mentors
items.body: Mentors are paid professionals with limited hours. We protect that time with clear formats, real context before each session and honest feedback channels.

campus.title: The digital campus for the future.
campus.body: Students explore. Mentors guide. AI assists. Projects demonstrate. Parents understand. Careers become clearer. That is the whole architecture — and v1 is the first honest slice of it, built around the six domains students actually asked for: AI, machine learning, robotics, drone technology, computer science and financial markets.
